messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — customer on‑prem reported cross-namespace pod-to-pod access after a control‑plane upgrade. Seems like a missing NetworkPolicy. Repro steps + logs attached. Can security + eng-sre triage? @sec-oncall
sec-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 created; priority P2. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-042
pat: On it. do we have the kube-proxy/CNI version details? Which CNI (calico/weave)?
alex: calico v3.21, kube 1.26, customer's using hostNetwork for a sidecar. Logs show iptables chains unexpectedly allowing FORWARD from ns-b to ns-a.
ingrid: HostNetworking sidecars are a common escape. First step: deny-by-default policy per namespace, then allow needed services. Patch we can push:
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-all-egress-ingress
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress
```
raj: Also check RBAC: any ClusterRoleBindings granted to serviceaccounts in the affected namespace? If SA has cluster-wide rights it could create pod with hostNetwork.
marta: From KMS side — do we see any suspicious key usage? Customer uses HSM via AWS KMS (cust-managed). Need audit trail for key usage during the window.
emily: Checked KMS audit for the window — no unusual decrypts. Only expected operator service account called Decrypt once at startup (CloudTrail shows operator-sa).
pat: Good. Next: enable verbose k8s audit for object-level changes for the timeframe. Add rule for pods/secrets/create and networkpolicies. Use existing policy skeleton: audit-policy-priv-deploy.yaml — I'll stage.
ingrid: Also recommend short-term mitigations for the customer: 1) remove hostNetwork from sidecars, 2) apply deny-all NetworkPolicy, 3) rotate any tokens/secrets exposed.
alex: Customer can't remove hostNetwork immediately; ask for a microsegmentation mitigation: create a namespace egress rule on host node iptables? Or taint nodes and move sidecars? Thoughts?
raj: Tainting might be heavy. We can use a NetworkPolicy with `namespaceSelector` to restrict ingress to only specific namespaces — lower blast radius and quick to apply.
marta: Also ensure KMS key rotation policy applied and logs shipped to their SIEM. We noticed the customer's rotation was disabled in the console.
ingrid: For longer term: add to onboarding checklist: deny-by-default NetworkPolicy, forbid hostNetwork in pod security admission, audit RBAC ClusterRoleBinding changes, and ensure KMS usage logs are forwarded and retained.
pat: I'll open a runbook: steps, commands, links to scripts. Can someone validate the NetworkPolicy patch before we push to customer cluster?
alex: I'll validate in staging and post results. If we see indicators of compromise (unexpected clusterrole creations) we'll escalate to IR. :exclamation:
sec-oncall: tagged.
sec-bot: Update: Incident severity elevated to P1 — cross-namespace compromise confirmed. Next: IR lead needed.
raj: I'm taking IR. Will collect etcd snapshot, api-server audit logs, kube-controller-manager logs. Ask customer to suspend any external CI/CD connectors until we have containment.
ingrid: Also check for leaked RBAC tokens in logs. Search api-audit.log for `impersonate` and `create clusterrolebinding` events, and grep etcd for unexpected secrets.
emily: Pushing a small helper script to query CloudTrail and KMS logs (https://git.redwood/tools/kms-audit-query).
alex: thanks all. keeping thread here. will ping when staging test complete. :thumbsup:
